heard: a comet once shown so brightly astronomers studied it in broad daylight. Discovered photographically by astronomer Richard M. West on August 10, 1975, the magnificent sun-grazer plummeted toward our star. By February 25, 1976, the cosmic visitor raced within exactly 30 million kilometers of the sun. Intense solar heating pushed its peak-apparent magnitude to minus 3, easily rivaling Venus. Observers watched in absolute amazement from February 25th to 27th as the dazzling object was clearly viewed under a full sun. Brutal tidal forces soon shattered the wandering ice block into four distinct pieces out in space. This daytime record proves comets can brilliantly outshine the daytime sky.
